messages:
maya: Hey team — noticed an odd throughput delta in last night's SKU sweep. L40S is ~12% slower than H100 for seq=8192 @ batch=1 on the small model we use for longctx smoke. numbers from the job below. anyone seen this pattern?

maya: job: bench/sku/nightly/241999 (link: https://ci.internal/bench/241999)

maya: sample output:
```
L40S - tokens/s: 340.2  (p50 0.5ms, p95 2.1ms)
H100  - tokens/s: 386.4  (p50 0.4ms, p95 1.8ms)
```

maya: config: `batch=1, kv_cache=on, q8_0`

sam: thanks for flagging — a few quick checks: was this run on a multi-tenant host? cache warmup complete? any nvlink errors in dmesg? :thinking_face:

maya: single-tenant host, warm cache (we ran 3 warm iterations before measuring). no kernel oops in syslog.

infra-bot: bench-runner: scheduled run completed. artifacts uploaded to https://s3.internal/bench/artifacts/241999 (size 23MB) :white_check_mark:

jess: I pulled the perf counters from the artifact. quick grep shows sustained mem_bw on L40S ~420 GB/s vs H100 ~470 GB/s during the long token phase. small but consistent.

leo: 420 vs 470 GB/s could explain 10-12% token/s difference for memory-bound kernels. did we force different CUDA/CuDNN kernels via compiled flags? also check pcie topology — L40S sometimes sits on a root complex with shared fabric that throttles in our lab racks.

sam: good call. @maya can you paste the runtime config (`REDWOOD_RUNTIME_FLAGS`) used for the job? also include `LD_PRELOAD` if any.

maya: here you go:
```
REDWOOD_RUNTIME_FLAGS="--kv-cache --quant=q8_0 --kernels=auto --batching=small"
LD_PRELOAD=""
```

maya: no special LD_PRELOAD. kernels=auto should pick optimal kernels.

nate: (reacts :eyes:) I noticed we recently changed a fallback path that prefers an AVX512-optimized host kernel for some binder ops — is it possible L40S hit fallback while H100 used the CUDA-prefixed path?

sam: that's possible. can you grep the logs for "fallback kernel" in the artifact?

jess: did that — found two fallback lines at step ~12000 tokens for L40S: `binder_op: falling back to host path (reason: kernel missing)` — H100 logs don't show that.

leo: ok that's a smoking gun. fallback to host path would be much slower and could be memory-latency sensitive. next steps: reproduce with verbose kernel selection on both SKUs and capture `nvprof`/`nsys` traces for the problematic stage.

maya: will run a targeted repro on both SKUs with `--kernel-verbose` and send traces. schedule preference: tonight's low-traffic window at 02:00 PT works for me.

sam: perfect. also capture `nvidia-smi dmon` and `nvlink --status` during the run. if we confirm fallback, we should add a guard in the kernel loader to blacklist that host fallback for longctx paths.

nate: I'll open a quick PR to force an error if kernel lookup fails for longctx-critical ops so we don't silently fall back. cc @jess for perf counters correlation.

jess: lgtm. once traces are up I can correlate cycles/mem_bw vs kernel names.

maya: thanks all — I'll post the verbose run artifacts here when done. ping me if you want to join the repro window. :thumbsup:

sam: leaving an action item: maya run verbose repro tonight; nate draft PR to make kernel-fallback audible; jess to do perf correlation; leo to check rack topology logs. will reconvene with traces. :calendar:
